title: Newsletter editor with zero coding experience drafts his tax filing with Claude Code
summary: Newsletter editor Shakeel Hashim, who doesn't code, had Claude Code draft his tax filing from bank statements and invoices; he says it "got everything right."
agent_role: Claude Code read local statements and invoices, categorized items and drafted the filing; Hashim reviewed the draft before filing.
outcome: Hashim says the draft "got everything right"
what_they_did: Shakeel Hashim, editor of the Transformer newsletter, says he has zero coding experience. Over two weeks he had Claude Code go through his bank statements and invoices to prepare a first draft of his tax filing. The Charter article quotes his post and gives no further detail on his steps.
how_it_went: Hashim wrote that the draft "got everything right."
prompt: I have my bank statements and invoices for [tax year] in [folder]. Read them and build a spreadsheet that lists every income and expense item with date, amount, source file and a suggested category for a [your country] tax filing as a [employee / freelancer / business type]. Flag anything you are unsure about or that might need a receipt. Then draft the figures for each section of my tax return and explain how you got each one. Do not submit or file anything. I will review the draft myself and check it with [a tax professional or official guidance].
